name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,817

entries.clue: Knot in net unravelled by fish (8)

indicatorNotes.unravelled: A net that is unravelled comes apart, so its letters come loose to be rearranged.
indicatorNotes.by: One thing placed by another sits next to it, so the second piece follows the first.

blocks.note: NET with its letters rearranged
to fish with a rod is to angle

annotation.surface: A fisherman finds a knot in his net that has come undone.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fish' looks like a noun in the net, but it is the verb: to angle. 'Knot' is a verb too, as in knotting string together.
annotation.definitionFit: To knot threads is to entangle them, twisting them together so they are caught.

entries.clue: Henry leaves rotten peaches in bunk (6)

indicatorNotes.leaves: When Henry leaves, his letter goes out of the word.
indicatorNotes.rotten: Rotten fruit has broken down, so the letters are spoilt into a new order.

blocks.note: H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance
PEACHES without its H

annotation.surface: Someone throws away rotten peaches found in a bed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bunk' looks like a bed for the peaches, but it is the British slang 'do a bunk', meaning run off.
annotation.definitionFit: In British slang a bunk is a sudden flight, as in 'do a bunk', which is an escape.

entries.clue: "What's one plus one?" read out in addition (3)

indicatorNotes.read out: Something read out is spoken, so the word is heard rather than seen.

blocks.note: the sum's answer, said aloud, is a number word; spell that sound another way

annotation.surface: A teacher reads a simple sum out to the class, as an extra question.
annotation.walkthrough: The quoted question looks like the whole puzzle, but its answer is only a stepping stone: the number said, then spelt as another word.
annotation.definitionFit: 'Too' means also, or in addition, as in 'me too'.

entries.clue: Authenticate, as opposed to issue (8)

blocks.note: 'X as opposed to Y' is 'X, not Y'
to issue from somewhere is to arise from it

annotation.surface: A clerk distinguishes certifying a document from merely issuing it.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Issue' sits in a surface about documents, where it means hand out; here it is the verb meaning come forth, as problems arise or issue.
annotation.definitionFit: A notary authenticates signatures and documents, and to notarise is to certify them that way.

entries.clue: Drink locked up by Cinderella's sisters (5)

indicatorNotes.locked up by: What is locked up by the words is held inside them, spanning the join.

blocks.note: the letters run across the join, from the end of Cinderella's into the start of sisters

annotation.surface: The ugly sisters keep a drink locked away from Cinderella.
annotation.walkthrough: A lassi is a yoghurt drink from South Asia.
annotation.definitionFit: A lassi is a drink of yoghurt thinned with water, sweet or salted.

entries.clue: Prudish editor ready for 12 to work on? (6)

blocks.note: prim = prudish, stiffly proper
ED is the standard abbreviation for editor

annotation.surface: A prim editor is ready for an artist's work to arrive.
annotation.walkthrough: 12 across is PORTRAIT PAINTER, and a canvas is primed with a base coat before the painter starts; the question mark flags that it is only one kind of readiness.
annotation.definitionFit: A primed canvas has had its undercoat and is ready for a painter to work on.

entries.clue: Keep shower curtains outside for event (6)

indicatorNotes.curtains: Curtains hang around a window, so the word curtains what goes inside it.
indicatorNotes.outside: The outside of a word is its first and last letters.

blocks.note: a shower is a brief fall of rain
the outer letters of EVENT

annotation.surface: Someone decides to hang on to the shower curtains for an occasion.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shower curtains' reads as one bathroom object; split it, and 'curtains' becomes a verb meaning hang round.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what you retain you hang on to rather than give up.

entries.clue: En route heading for Nepal, am I excited? (11)

annotation.definition: En route heading for Nepal, am I excited?

indicatorNotes.heading for: The heading of a word is its first letter.
indicatorNotes.excited: Excited particles are agitated, so the letters are stirred into a new order.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
the first letter of Nepal
anagram fodder, 3 letters

annotation.surface: A traveller on the way to Nepal wonders whether they are thrilled.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the description: someone en route for Nepal, excited, is a climber on the way to the Himalayas.
annotation.definitionFit: Nepal is home to Everest, so the eager traveller heading there is most likely a mountaineer.

entries.clue: Separate daughters can be found on island (8)

blocks.note: d is the abbreviation for daughter, as in family trees
is in the sense of exists, is to be found: what can be found somewhere is there
Crete, the Greek island

annotation.surface: Some daughters are said to be found living on an island.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Separate' looks like a verb in front of the daughters, but it is the adjective meaning distinct.
annotation.definitionFit: Discrete means individually separate and distinct, as in discrete parts.

entries.clue: Jump on insects, getting tons inside shorts (3,5)

indicatorNotes.on: In a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so it comes first.
indicatorNotes.inside: What is inside goes within the other word.

blocks.note: a hop is a small jump
T is the abbreviation for ton or tons
ants, the standard crossword insects

annotation.surface: Someone leaps on a swarm of insects, and some end up down their shorts.
annotation.walkthrough: The tons go into the jump, not into the insects: 'getting tons inside' belongs to the first word of the clue.
annotation.definitionFit: Hot pants are very short, tight shorts, a fashion of the early 1970s.

entries.clue: Deal a heavy blow to Conservative boor (5)

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for Conservative, the British political party
a lout is a rough, boorish man

annotation.surface: Someone wants to thump a Tory lout.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Deal a heavy blow to' reads as what happens to the boor, but it is the definition, and 'to' belongs to it.
annotation.definitionFit: To clout someone is to hit them hard, a heavy blow with the hand.

entries.clue: Spooner's bench closes rat runs (5,4)

indicatorNotes.Spooner's: The Reverend Spooner was famous for swapping the opening sounds of two words, so the pair named here trade their fronts.

blocks.note: the bench is the judges, and so a court of law; its front sound swaps with the next word's
what closes shuts; it trades its SH for the K sound

annotation.surface: A court is adjourned while rats scurry about the building.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bench' is the legal sense, the judges or magistrates sitting, which makes it a court. A rat run is British for a side-street route drivers use to dodge main-road traffic.
annotation.definitionFit: A rat run is a back-street short cut used by drivers to avoid congestion.

entries.clue: Supplier of commemorative mugs? (8,7)

blocks.note: the surface pictures a maker of souvenir crockery; the setter means someone whose trade produces the objects
mug is slang for face, and a painting of a face records its sitter for posterity

annotation.surface: A souvenir shop sells mugs marking a royal occasion.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface points at a souvenir-mug maker; 'mug' is slang for a face, and the question mark admits the pun.
annotation.definitionFit: A portrait painter supplies faces, or mugs, painted to commemorate their sitters.

entries.clue: Trainer with acne rocks back with a new body (11)

indicatorNotes.rocks: What rocks is shaken back and forth, and the letters are jolted into a new order.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram fodder, 4 letters

annotation.surface: A spotty gym trainer has come back with a whole new physique.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back with a new body' looks like a gym success story, and it is the definition: returned to life in another form.
annotation.definitionFit: Reincarnate, as an adjective, means reborn in a new body after death.

entries.clue: Fresh, popular part of the English Channel (8)

blocks.note: what is popular is in
the Solent is the strait between the Isle of Wight and the English mainland

annotation.surface: A travel note about a lively, well-loved stretch of the English Channel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fresh' sits beside the sea as if it meant bracing; it means cheeky.
annotation.definitionFit: A fresh remark is a cheeky one, rude to a superior, which is insolent.

entries.clue: Start of flood eventually surrounding old hollow willow (3,5)

indicatorNotes.surrounding: One word surrounding others is placed around them.
indicatorNotes.hollow: A hollow word has had its middle scooped out, leaving only its outside letters.

blocks.note: what happens eventually happens later
O is the abbreviation for old
the outer letters of WILLOW

annotation.surface: A flood slowly engulfs an ancient hollow willow tree.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Start of flood' looks like an instruction to take F; it is the definition, the flood tide that begins at the lowest point of the ebb.
annotation.definitionFit: Tides ebb to low water and then the flood, the incoming tide, begins there.

entries.clue: Meaning there's no difference between gin and tonic? (4)

blocks.note: the first letter of gin, as the drink is written G and T
saying one thing is another says there is no difference between them
the first letter of tonic, the other half of G and T

annotation.surface: Someone asks whether gin and tonic taste any different from each other.
annotation.walkthrough: A gin and tonic is written G and T, and 'no difference between' them makes the sentence G is T.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of drift: getting someone's meaning is catching the main point of what they say.

entries.clue: The price of litigation about bum crackers goes up (8)

indicatorNotes.about: One word about another goes around it.
indicatorNotes.crackers: Crackers means mad, so the letters go wild and rearrange.

blocks.note: the loser in a lawsuit is ordered to pay costs
BUM with its letters rearranged

annotation.surface: Legal fees soar after a lawsuit over firecrackers.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Crackers goes up' reads as fireworks, but 'crackers' only scrambles BUM; 'goes up', in flames, is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Something that combusts catches fire and goes up in flames.

entries.clue: Two murders, the highest price paid (3,5)

blocks.note: to top someone is slang for kill them; this is the first murder
to whack someone is gangster slang for kill; the second murder

annotation.surface: A contract killer is paid the top rate for a double hit.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Two murders' gives two slang words for kill, placed one after the other. Top whack is British slang for the maximum price or rate.
annotation.definitionFit: British slang: paying top whack means paying the highest price going.

entries.clue: Before church, after running (4)

indicatorNotes.after: The first piece comes after the second, so the order is swapped from how the clue reads.

blocks.note: a machine that is running is on
CE is the Church of England

annotation.surface: A jogger's timetable: a run, then church.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Before' and 'after' look like a matching pair of order words; only 'after' is, and 'Before' is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: Once means formerly, at some time before, as in 'once a mill town'.

entries.clue: Wife aboard scooter turning forty (3-5)

indicatorNotes.aboard: Someone aboard a vehicle is inside it.
indicatorNotes.turning: A scooter turning spins round, and its letters turn into a new order.

blocks.note: W is the abbreviation for wife
anagram fodder, 7 letters

annotation.surface: A wife celebrates turning forty on the back of a scooter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Turning forty' reads as a birthday, but 'turning' scrambles the scooter; 'forty' stands alone as the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: An old counting word: a score is twenty, as in the Bible's threescore years and ten.

entries.clue: Gift of story books (6)

blocks.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

annotation.surface: A present of a book of stories.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Gift' reads as a present in a bookshop surface; it means a natural ability.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an ability someone is born with, as in 'she has a gift for languages'.

entries.clue: Cast wanting seat for Lear in the audience? (6)

indicatorNotes.in the audience: What the audience gets is what it hears, so the word is taken by its sound.

blocks.note: Lear is a king, and a king's seat is his throne

annotation.surface: A theatre company's cast lacks a chair for King Lear, watched by the audience.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like the actors in a play about Lear, but it is the past participle of cast, as in thrown.
annotation.definitionFit: Cast, as a past participle, means thrown, as a stone is cast or thrown.

entries.clue: Paired blocks I see, record price for a British sculptor (7,8)

blocks.note: a bar is a block, as of chocolate or soap; two of them
'ah' is what you say when you see what someone means
an EP is an extended-play record
a thing's worth is its price

annotation.surface: Someone notes a record price paid for a pair of blocks by a sculptor.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Record price' reads as an auction headline; split it into a disc and a value. Barbara Hepworth was an English modernist sculptor, known for pierced stone and bronze forms.
annotation.definitionFit: Barbara Hepworth (1903-1975) was an English sculptor, one of the leading British modernists.

entries.clue: More sculpture, perhaps by European from the south (5)

indicatorNotes.from the south: In a down clue, reading from the south means reading from the bottom up.

blocks.note: sculpture is one example of art
X means by, as in 3 by 4
E is the abbreviation for European

annotation.surface: More sculpture by a European artist is coming up from the south.
annotation.walkthrough: 'By' looks like it names the sculptor; here it is the multiplication sign, as in measurements.
annotation.definitionFit: Extra means more than usual or additional.

entries.clue: Coach went right to the house (5,4)

blocks.note: a stagecoach, or stage for short
someone who went has left

annotation.surface: A coach turned right towards the house.
annotation.walkthrough: 'House' is the theatre audience. Stage left is the actor's left as they face the audience, so it is the audience's right.
annotation.definitionFit: Stage directions are given from the actor's side, so stage left is on the right as seen from the house.

entries.clue: Jamaican choked eating Mexican chilli (5)

indicatorNotes.eating: The words are eating the answer: it is held inside them.

blocks.note: the letters span the join, from the end of Jamaican into the start of choked

annotation.surface: A Jamaican chokes on a hot Mexican chilli.
annotation.walkthrough: The heat of the surface is what makes the choking plausible. An ancho is a dried poblano pepper.
annotation.definitionFit: The ancho is a mild Mexican chilli, the dried form of the poblano.

entries.clue: Nick's pretty short of energy (3)

indicatorNotes.short of: A word short of something lacks it, so that letter is taken away.

blocks.note: cute = pretty
E is the symbol for energy

annotation.surface: Someone called Nick is rather good-looking, if a little lacking in energy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nick' reads as a man's name; it is a small cut, as in nicking yourself shaving.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a small notch in the skin or an edge, as when you nick yourself shaving.

entries.clue: Be a dick, hustle vagrant (6)

indicatorNotes.vagrant: A vagrant wanders, so the letters wander out of order.

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 6 letters

annotation.surface: An insult: don't be rude and pester a tramp.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Dick' is old American slang for a detective, a private dick, so being one is playing detective.
annotation.definitionFit: To sleuth is to investigate like a detective, and a dick is slang for a detective.

entries.clue: Stop the heaviest rugby players? I can (4,2,2)

blocks.note: the pack is a rugby team's forwards, its biggest players
I, carried straight through
a can is a tin

annotation.surface: A rugby player boasts he can halt the opposing forwards.
annotation.walkthrough: 'I can' reads as a boast; it is two pieces, I and a tin can.
annotation.definitionFit: To pack it in is British slang for stop doing something, or give up.
